findings.title: Discoverability surface names `sq model list`, which is not the command
findings.description: The design specifies the model-list marker and its verification against `sq model list` (lines 37, 82, 112, 173, 180, 205, 211, 223). Slice 928 explicitly established the opposite: "`sq model list` … does not exist — the command is `sq models list`" and fixed it "in both command trees" (928-slice...md:24, :44). Source confirms: `src/squadron/cli/app.py:55` registers the app as `name="models"` and `src/squadron/cli/commands/models.py:193` defines `@models_app.command("list")` — the real command is `sq models list`. The verification walkthrough step ("`sq model list` → `codex-agent` and `codex-spark` marked") cannot pass as written, and the README instruction would name a non-existent command. The slice-plan entry carries the same stale name, but the design is where the executable surface is defined. Rename throughout to `sq models list`.

findings.title: Logout and pre-auth CLI paths have no enumerated failure modes
findings.description:
The "Failure Modes — Codex Turn" table (lines 116–135) is thorough for the turn path — hang, timeout, transport closed mid-turn, server busy, auth rejected, empty response, absent usage, teardown — and the login `wait()` and `account()` paths each get a row and a timeout key (D7, lines 107–109). But two new I/O paths the design itself introduces are uncovered:

- **`sq auth logout`** spawns the runtime per the design's own statement ("Spawning is confined to three places — a Codex turn, `sq auth login/logout`, and `sq auth status`", line 82) and calls `AsyncCodex.logout()` (line 54, D3). There is no row for: runtime fails to start, `logout()` raises, hang (no `codex.logout_timeout_s` in the D7 table), or transport close. Success criterion "…`sq auth logout openai-oauth` removes the login" (line 192) and walkthrough step 8 assert the happy path only.
- **`sq auth login`/`logout` when `openai_codex` is not installed.** The install-hint row is scoped "at `create_agent`" (line 118). The Value section promises "A missing piece is named at the point of failure with the exact command to fix it" (line 24), but the login/logout path through `login.py` is never stated to route through `resolve_codex_runtime()` or its hint — `resolve_codex_runtime()`'s described callers are agent, provider, and doctor (D2/D9).

Add rows (and, for logout, a timeout bound) covering these, or state explicitly that logout reuses the turn-path handling and the `ExtraRequirement` hint.

findings.title: D1 pins `<1` while calling the upper bound undecided
findings.description: D1's spec string is `codex = ["openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1"]` — a decided cap — but the same bullet says "the upper bound is a PM call" and Special Considerations (line 231) says "not decided here … PM to say whether to cap." One of the two must go: either keep `<1` and drop the open question, or leave the spec as `>=0.159.3` until the PM decides. As written the implementer has both a bound and a statement that the bound is not decided.

findings.title: Architecture auth-model handling is sound; the deferred edit is acceptable
findings.description: The dedicated section correctly identifies that `InteractiveLogin` is net-new relative to `100-arch.orchestration-v2.md`'s "Squadron does not attempt to unify authentication" (arch line 243) and argues it unifies nothing: it is an optional capability with one implementer, credentials stay in `~/.codex/auth.json`, and the CLI dispatch is capability-based (`isinstance`), consistent with slice 128's capabilities-over-identity rule. I verified the argument against the architecture text and find no layer violation or dependency inversion — `providers/auth.py` gains a Protocol, `cli` depends on it, `providers/codex/auth.py` implements it, and nothing in `core` learns about credentials. Deferring the arch sentence until a second provider adopts interactive login is proportionate.
